title: You can finally use Google Gemini to control your MacBook
body: Google and Apple might be competitors, but they can play nice sometimes. For example, Google just announced that you can now use Gemini AI to control a Mac computer. With this new feature, you can give Gemini commands and it will root through your files, access your apps, and browse the web to complete whatever tasks you've asked it to perform. All of this is facilitated by the Gemini app for macOS 27 Golden Gate, per Google's press release. SEE ALSO: Google commemorates Robert Pattinson's James Bond casting with a sneaky Easter egg How can users take advantage of Gemini computer use for MacBooks, Mac Mini, and iMac devices? Google provided several examples in an announcement blog post, such as asking Gemini to take a child's sketch of a butterfly and render it polygonally using the 3D modeling program Blender. Once the request is processed, Gemini performs the task in an isolated background window with a preview display right in the Gemini app, allowing you to watch it perform the task in real-time. However, as Google noted, you also retain full use of your Mac while this is happening, allowing users to continue browsing, typing, and completing other types of work. While this may be a boon to Gemini power users who own devices like the new MacBook Pro OLED , it's worth noting that giving an AI agent full access to all your local files and apps carries inherent risks. Google gives users the ability to freely choose which apps Gemini has access to, alongside the ability to watch the process as it unfolds, in case something goes wrong. title: Dont worry, Artificials unsettling AI poster was actually made by a human
body: NEON has released a new poster for Luca Guadagnino's upcoming OpenAI film Artificial , and the visual is peak uncanny valley. SEE ALSO: 'Artificial' review: Andrew Garfield enters his villain era The illustrated poster centers on Andrew Garfield as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who stands in a redwood forest overlooking San Francisco Bay. He holds out a hand, inviting us into an unknown future. View this post on Instagram For anyone who's ever wanted to go hiking with Garfield, the image seems like a dream come true. But stare at the poster for more than one second, and your brain starts to reject everything that's in front of it. Why does that redwood have a face? Why is a grassy hill glitching into a tunnel? Why does Altman look like he's about to call me "Spider Monkey" and take me on a piggyback ride through the woods, Edward Cullen-style? Most importantly: Why does everything carry the discomforting sheen of AI? Could NEON have missed the point of Artificial 's cautionary tale entirely and made promotional materials using AI? Don't panic. A line of text alongside the bottom right edge of the poster affirms that the artwork was made by humans. To back that affirmation up, NEON also released a video of the poster being digitally illustrated, tagging creative agency Gravillis Inc. and artist Mike Thompson. View this post on Instagram Comments under NEON's initial post of the poster appreciated the clever AI-adjacent marketing tactic. title: Fiona the hippo, one of the internets most beloved animal icons, has died
body: Fiona, the beloved Cincinnati Zoo hippo who became an internet sensation after surviving a premature birth in 2017, has died at age 9. The zoo announced Thursday that Fiona died after accidentally swallowing a knit hat that fell into her enclosure earlier this month, despite days of intensive veterinary care. Her death has prompted an outpouring of grief online from fans who watched her grow from a vulnerable 29-pound newborn into one of the internet's most recognizable animal celebrities. Born six weeks premature, Fiona became a viral sensation as the Cincinnati Zoo documented her unlikely survival on social media. Millions followed her progress, celebrating everything from her first steps to her swimming lessons. Nearly a decade later, she remained a beloved fixture of internet culture, inspiring memes, merchandise, and a devoted online following. Nearly a decade later, the internet is mourning her loss. The Cincinnati Zoo confirmed her death in a heartbreaking statement, explaining that its veterinary team had spent days attempting to help Fiona pass the foreign object. Despite round-the-clock care and multiple treatments, her condition deteriorated. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. "We are in shock at the moment," Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement, as reported by the BBC . "We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn't anymore." title: Microsoft CEO explains reason behind the 60,000 buyouts (its AI, of course)
body: Last month, Microsoft asked as many as 60,000 employees to voluntarily leave their jobs with buyout offers. This week, CEO Satya Nadella took some time to explain why. In a talk with Andrew Ross Sorkin at the New York Times ' DealBook Summit in New York City (as reported by TechCrunch ), Nadella addressed the buyout offer that made headlines in October. As we reported at the time, the buyouts came amidst a huge amount of AI investment at Microsoft and industry-wide AI layoffs . And in his comments at the summit, Nadella made it explicitly clear that the company reorganization was necessary because of AI. You can listen to the CEO's full comments at about 27:20 in the New York Times' YouTube video of the interview : SEE ALSO: Microsoft outage cause revealed: It was a perfect storm of problems According to Nadella, it's not necessarily about directly replacing humans with AI in a one-to-one fashion. However, that may not be comforting to workers asked to leave their jobs, if only voluntarily. Let s take software engineering. We went from, Well, we don t buy that AI can ever do software. To suddenly, Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers? To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point, Nadella said. The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates. Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday . He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.” Evasive and irregular turns “FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.” Read full article Comments

It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman. body: Blue Origin announced Thursday that its New Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029 as part of that company's Project Suncatcher program. Google disclosed it was working on scalable orbiting data centers about a year ago and characterized the project as one of its research "moonshots." The mission on New Glenn is designed to deploy satellites, each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack, into Sun-synchronous orbit where they can receive nearly continuous solar energy. title: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
author: Scott K. Johnson
body: Many studies over the years have examined how people encounter climate science information. Some focused on the top results that Google surfaced (back when Google was still in the business of serving links), while others examined social media content or newspaper and TV news coverage. With large language models (LLMs) now forming a share of the public information diet, it's worth looking at how they handle climate change. But there’s no direct way for researchers to look at the information people have seen. It is served ephemerally to individual users, confined to their chat session. A study led by researchers from University College London and the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) tried to tackle this question from multiple angles, testing LLMs with different prompts and evaluating their output. They started with benchmarks of simple factual questions (benchmarks that might even be in models’ training data at this point) but also analyzed more complex interactions—including when users think they’re right to push back on an answer. CO 2 Q A LLM research often faces ( no-true-Scotsman-tinged ) criticism for focusing on a particular model rather than some other frontier model that may have been released after the experiment concluded. In this case, the study used 33 models, including multiple versions of the major frontier and open-weight models. The flagship frontier models used were Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Gemini 3.6 Flash, and GPT-5.6 Sol. (You can find the full list in the report .) Read full article

title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Google announced Android developer verification last year , and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead . It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven't registered their apps to do so soon. The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google's new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won't be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure . Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps. In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it's not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within "several months." title: The rumored OLED iMac may be canceled or delayed
body: Apple just launched a new iMac in October, but rumors are already swirling about the next one, and they're not entirely positive. The Elec reported on Thursday that Apple is considering delaying or even canceling a hypothetical OLED-equipped iMac model, which was theoretically supposed to launch in 2029 or 2030. According to the report, which cited an unnamed industry source, Apple has been working with Samsung Display (a prolific supplier of device displays) on the project, and has been discussing a potential delay or cancellation with the Korean firm. "For now, discussions are focused on delaying the schedule and monitoring market conditions," an anonymous industry official said, per The Elec. Unsurprisingly, money seems like the biggest factor here. Apple is reportedly concerned about the cost of equipping its all-in-one desktop computers with fancy (but expensive) OLED displays, given that iMacs don't sell at nearly the same volume as some of Apple's other flagship products, like the iPhone. The Elec also cited weak sales of the iPad Pro , which has a ProMotion OLED display, as a factor here. SEE ALSO: Apple's iPhone Duo gets Face ID, sort of Given that Apple also has a new CEO as of September, it makes sense that some plans made under Tim Cook's direction might be reconsidered now that John Ternus is in charge. While an OLED iMac would certainly turn some heads, it also makes sense that these plans are for three or four years from now. title: Mouse fight club might explain why we like to watch violent things
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 There's something about watching violent events that broadly appeals to us, whether it's the latest John Wick movie, a video game, or a live UFC bout. Scientists have debated whether watching violent things could make us more aggressive, but it could also be an adaptive survival strategy. Male mice, for instance, who watch other mice fighting learned enough about how to fight to better protect themselves (compared to mice who didn't watch fights) when pitted against stronger, more aggressive opponents, according to a paper published in the journal Nature. The team assigned male mice randomly to three different groups—fighters, spectators, or novices—and then subjected each group to eight days of training involving three 10-minute sessions per day. The novices played with stuffed mice in isolation, while the spectators watched various pairs of fighter mice battle it out from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier—a set-up chosen to let them smell and listen to the fights as well as observe them. The ninth day was "fight night," when all the mice had to face a daunting opponent in three 4-minute rounds. Each fight was filmed from above so that the mouse behavior could be analyzed. To monitor corresponding changes in brain activity, the team engineered the rodents' excitatory brain cells to glow green whenever they were activated, while inhibitory brain cells glowed red. title: NASA's new Moon plans have a problem: Orion wasn't designed to fly this way
author: Eric Berger
body: NASA recently announced a significant shakeup to the Artemis program that will land humans on the Moon. The moves were designed to give the agency's lunar lander providers—SpaceX with its Starship vehicle, and Blue Origin with Blue Moon—more flexibility in reaching the Moon. For Starship, this means docking with Orion in Earth orbit, and then traveling to the Moon in tandem. For Blue Moon, it shifts the rendezvous with Orion all the way to low-lunar orbit. These changes benefit the lunar landers, but in turn impose more of a burden on the Orion spacecraft, which is built for NASA by Lockheed Martin. In 2026, lines outside stores are practically nonexistent. We certainly can't see them. While major retailers will be running holiday sales throughout all of November, savvy shoppers know that Black Friday and Cyber Monday (and the few days surrounding them) still remain the absolute biggest shopping days of the year for their ability to reliably trigger record-low prices on big-ticket items (like TVs , Apple devices , smartwatches , headphones , and of course, Amazon's own devices ) . That includes discounts that beat Amazon's massively hyped October Prime Day deals. title: How to tell a cyberattack from a plain old outage
author: Andy Greenberg, wired.com
body: Over the past week, anyone could be forgiven for wondering whether a Diehard IV –style cyberwar had finally arrived in the US. Across just four consecutive business days, a mass Microsoft exchange outage broke IT services for thousands of companies , a Federal Aviation Administration tech screw-up grounded airplanes across the country, a software problem affecting JPMorgan Chase caused another round of disruption, a United Airlines system glitch delayed flights yet again, and an NSA classified network’s downtime left the agency’s staff sitting at home waiting to return to their office at Fort Meade. In the midst of a US war with Iran and rising fears of AI-enabled hacking , this still-unfolding comedy of IT errors colliding across American infrastructure felt to plenty of observers like more than a coincidence. Yet there’s still no evidence that any one of these clustered technological failures were related, much less caused by hackers. Their improbable, sequential timing left Americans anxiously doomscrolling for signs of foul play. But in cases like these, it’s the job of cybersecurity analysts (and reporters at WIRED) to determine—vibes aside—whether the latest tech outage was actually an accident or the result of a cyberattack. body: If you like playing daily word games like Wordle , then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine. There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown. An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle. title: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in. On the nights of November 15 and November 16, coordinated waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles caused enough damage to collapse one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an Institute for the Study of War update . Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile. The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times . Each networked drone acts as a relay node to extend the communication link between human operators and remotely piloted missiles and strike drones. Russia began using the technique to support long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities. Read full article Comments

title: Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick
author: Beth Mole
body: In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump's pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation. Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy's decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats. In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA's current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn't say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is "quite lethal" or that children are given vaccine doses the "size of a soda bottle." Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong. Read full article Comments

title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
author: Nick Indge
body: Microsoft's Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core . Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency's (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG). STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: "The s ecure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened. " The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance. Read full article Comments

title: A Scattered Spider hacker just got 6 years in a U.S. prison
body: Scattered Spider was once called "one of the most dangerous financial criminal groups" by Microsoft cybersecurity researchers. The U.S. has now closed the case against five of the group's members, sending the final defendant to prison for more than half a decade. British Scattered Spider member Tyler Robert Buchanan has just been sentenced to six years in prison, according to the DOJ. Buchanan, who is 24 years old, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. SEE ALSO: What is 'Scattered Spider'? How this massive phishing scam worked. The five Scattered Spider hackers took part in a massive phishing campaign which targeted employees of major technology companies, telecommunications companies, and entertainment companies between September 2021 and April 2023. During this time, Scattered Spider carried out a massive phishing scheme where they posed as employers or their IT providers, spamming employees with text messages that urged them to log in to phishing websites. Once the victims logged in, Scattered Spider hackers weaponized these stolen credentials in order to access employees' accounts and their employers' computer systems. The hackers took confidential business information and individuals' credentials and private data. Using this information, Scattered Spider also deployed SIM-swapping attacks which resulted in the hackers stealing at least $11.6 million from cryptocurrency wallets. title: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status
author: Beth Mole
body: International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings. After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it " shameful " and a " national embarrassment ." News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases , more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases . There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week. But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What's happening now is a runaway epidemic. Read full article Comments

title: The future of tech will not be inclusive by default
body: Ten years ago, QueerTech began with a feeling that too many 2SLGBTQI+ people in the technology sector know well: not belonging. My co-founder Andy Salda a and I were working at different companies in tech and kept running into the same frustration. We could see the possibility of the sector around us, had the skills to succeed, and believed technology, when stewarded responsibly, could change lives. Yet we could not see a place for ourselves, as queer professionals, within it. I grew up in Morocco, where being queer was, and continues to be, illegal. In 2007, I left for New York City in pursuit of the "American Dream." There, I quickly realized this dream was based on a contradiction opportunity without equal rights. Finally, I moved to Montreal, drawn to Canada s reputation for respecting people across cultures, religions, and identities. SEE ALSO: Meta is allegedly deleting LGBTQ and plus-sized business Instagram accounts Across this journey, I expected geography to change my sense of belonging. It never did. So in 2016, Andy and I started small. QueerTech was a volunteer-run community group built around a simple need: to find one another, create connections, and make space for queer people in an industry where many of us felt invisible. title: Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories
author: Kyle Orland
body: The computer gaming world hasn't heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity , The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright's subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA . Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players' memories. MyMems , which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright's previous projects by "turn[ing] the simulation inward," as Wright's Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning . The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world. “If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?" Wright says by way of example in the release. "If I had to build a bridge across a short chasm, which three people from my life would I choose to help me?" Read full article Comments

title: It shouldn’t be this easy to pedal 25 mph: Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo
author: Jacob May
body: I’ve had only one experience of pedaling an e-bike after it ran out of juice, but it was enough to make checking the battery display an anxiety-driven habit: “Can I afford to use the highest assist level up this hill? Should I switch to eco mode to preserve power and make sure I have enough to get home with the bike lights on?” These aren’t fun questions to have rattling around in your head while riding home in the dark. But those intrusive thoughts never crossed my mind while I was testing Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo . I didn't experience range anxiety, even while blowing through city streets at 25-plus mph (40.2 kph). The bike has so much juice (840 watt-hours) and power (810 watts of peak power and 105 newton-meters of torque) from Specialized's 3.1 motor system that I could ride as far and as fast as I wanted without worrying about having enough battery to get back home. title: 175+ major websites affected by malware hack, report says: What we know
body: The past several days have seen non-stop outages at Microsoft , Chase Bank , and Apple , to name a few. Fitting with that theme, cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme published a report on Monday detailing a malware infection that he said affected more than 175 major websites, including CNN, Zoom, Equifax, Ikea, and Peacock. You can check out Helme's full report at Report URI for all of the granular details, but the hackers were reportedly able to compromise those sites with malware through a third-party platform called Optimizely, which creates popular tools for testing websites. SEE ALSO: Apple confirms iCloud sign-in issues, App Store and Apple Pay outages The simple version of the story is that the hackers inserted malicious JavaScript into some customer projects. This malware was designed to swap cryptocurrency wallet information with the attackers', steal cookies and screenshots, and skim payment info. The hackers also targeted visitors using older iPhones and iPads, according to Helme's report. The headline news is alarming malware reportedly made its way to popular websites people visit every day but the researcher found that the attackers' crypto wallets only contained about $7,000, all of which was transferred during a nine-hour time period on Nov. 16. And just because malware appeared on a site, that doesn't necessarily mean that hackers successfully exploited visitors to that sites. title: YouTube will now guess how many people are co-viewing on TV
body: YouTube is making another big change to how views are counted on long-form videos, YouTube Shorts, and livestreams. According to a company update , YouTube will now include "co-views" in public video view counts. What is a co-view? It's YouTube's estimate of how many people are watching content together on TV via a single account. YouTube says it will include these estimated views because "viewers are now watching over 1 billion hours of YouTube on TVs every day." The company says it wants to "credit creators true reach" and "provide a more complete picture of how audiences are engaging with content." SEE ALSO: Is YouTube getting a separate social networking app? This isn't the first recent change to how YouTube counts video views. This past summer, the platform started counting views from the moment a video plays. Previously, viewers had to watch for a specific amount of time, typically around 30 seconds for long-form videos, in order for their view to be counted in the public metric. Co-views is certainly a bit more offbeat than that, as the company is essentially inflating view counts by estimating how many people are watching together on a single device that would've previously been counted as a single view. YouTube, however, says this new platform metric "aligns with TV industry standards, including how traditional broadcast and streaming networks estimate the total number of people exposed to content." title: GTA 6 cheat codes: There are cheats, but theres a catch
body: Throughout their storied history, the Grand Theft Auto games have usually allowed players to skip the stuff they don't like by using cheat codes. There have been codes to inflate in-game wallets, unlock every gun, and even spawn the best vehicles out of thin air. This time, GTA 6 cheat codes take the franchise in a new direction. Developer Rockstar Games has, by all accounts , created a GTA game that's at least trying to be a little more serious, sincere, and heartfelt than its predecessors. As such, you cannot simply bust out the "all guns" cheat from the start of the game and go on a rampage. According to PC Gamer , the game does have cheats, but they are only accessible after completing all 91 main story missions. SEE ALSO: Rockstar hints massive 'GTA 6' map saved room for future content 6 Yes, you have to roll credits on the story to use the GTA 6 cheats. Don't get mad at us, get mad at Rockstar. PC Gamer confirmed that these cheats can't be used in an early-game save, and activating them will prevent the player from saving from that point on. What's even more interesting: Beating the game doesn't immediately let you use the cheats in question; it merely lets you see a list of them, each with a corresponding in-game challenge that needs to be completed before they can be used. Once a cheat is unlocked, it can then be activated by opening the in-game phone, holding L1 and pressing R1 (or LB and RB on Xbox), and then inputting specific button combos. "ULA has completed an initial integrated review of flight data from the Leo 1 launch anomaly that occurred last Sunday," the company said in a statement . "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines." title: Waymo has stopped its robotaxis from driving on the freeway—here’s why
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Waymo is currently restricting its fleet of robotaxis to surface streets after getting into hot water with California over its cars' driving behavior on highways. Specifically, the software tends to drive into construction zones at speed. As first reported by the San Francisco Business Times , this behavior actually drew the ire of California’s DMV earlier this month, which ordered Waymo to stop driving on Californian highways immediately and until it can convince the DMV that its cars no longer “pose an imminent hazard to public safety.” This is not Waymo’s first run-in with this problem. In Arizona, Waymo robotaxis did not recognize ramp closure signs on six occasions in Phoenix in April and entered construction zones. A month later in California, seven Waymo robotaxis entered lanes with active construction. In June, Waymo recalled the almost 3,800 robotaxis capable of highway driving. That problem led Waymo to stick to surface streets only in California after the May incidents until late July, when the robotaxis resumed highway operations. In early July, Waymo told the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration that it began updating the robotaxi software to a version that “improve[s] the recognition of freeway construction zones, more appropriately prioritize[s] construction zones over other freeway hazards, and reduce[s] speed when the AV detects that it may be in a construction zone.” Read full article Comments

title: What is the possibility couple? Gen Z may be ushering in a new trend.
body: Dating optimism might be in, and not just because of the recent "blue wave." In its latest D.A.T.E. Report (Data, Advice, Trends, and Expertise), called Dating While Dreaming Big, Hinge found some hope in daters. Gen Z singles are seeing possibility in their future partners and how they can lead to their ideal future selves. Seventy-six percent of Gen Z imagine the person they want to become alongside their ideal partner, according to Hinge's July 2026 survey of over 13,000 people around the world, including Gen Z and millennial daters. One in four members of Gen Z (25 percent) is more likely than millennials to believe their ideal partner will help them achieve their ideal life, while two out of three (67 percent) prefer a partner who makes them feel hopeful and inspired. SEE ALSO: AI agents are banned on Tinder and Hinge, CEO says Only seven percent of Gen Z believe they'll achieve their life goals on their own, signaling that young adults want to enter a power couple of sorts. Or, maybe, what Hinge has coined as "the possibility couple," or a relationship where being together makes you feel more hopeful about the future. But with all this optimism comes the pressure to find the perfect partner...which doesn't exist. And this is compounded by ever-growing uncertainty. Costs are high and don't seem to be going down, while the AI industry threatens to eat all of our jobs. title: How The Verge is picking which Black Friday deals to share
body: For the past month, we’ve been inundated with Black Friday deals, signaling what’s to come on the biggest shopping day of the year in the US. We routinely get dozens of press releases a day, coming from brands big and small that hope that we’ll publicize these offers. Of course, the companies would prefer that we don’t do any research on these deals to see if they’re actually good, and most don’t provide any of the necessary context we’re looking for when vetting them. Most indicators of a good deal are confusing — not just for us, but for anyone who’s shopping. Groundwork Collaborative recently published its findings about the unclear manner in which Amazon displays deals. Its researchers tracked a selection of products ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday in 2024 and 2025, and they claim that nearly one in three products advertised as deals on Amazon didn’t offer savings during the actual shopping events. The investigation also found that nearly a tenth of the deals it examined were more expensive during the sales events than on some days in the month leading up to them. Something we commonly see on Amazon and attempt to correct for in our coverage are good deals with inflated discount claims. As in, the original retail amount (the “list” price) is sometimes higher than the usual day-to-day price to make the savings seem more substantial. Sometimes, the manufacturer’s suggested retail price (MSRP) is what’s shown, though that’s not always the case. title: Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details
author: Robert Pearlman
body: In the one light-day that humanity's most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again. Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter's moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a "commemorative phonograph record," in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space. About those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson . While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs' overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago. title: GTA 6 is the highest-rated game of all time
body: Grand Theft Auto VI is officially out and critics love it . Unleashed on Wednesday 13 years after its predecessor, Rockstar Games' wildly anticipated game has landed the highest ever rating on Metacritic . Essentially, it's instantly the best-reviewed game of all time, according to the aggregator site. SEE ALSO: 'GTA 6' reviews are in: What's the verdict? GTA 6 has a 99 percent rating on Metacritic, based on 147 critic reviews. This is a weighted average of individual critic scores calculated by Metacritic staff through a complex system involving review detail, publication prestige, and whether the critic has provided a score in their review. Well, I think they like it. Credit: Mashable screenshot: Metacritic Metacritic predicted GTA 6 would average 96 percent, an already staggering number it's blown out of the water. In a dramatic twist, GTA 6 also accelerated past the previous #1 ranked game of all time , 1998 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , which has just dominated headlines with Nintendo's new remastered version . The top two highest ranked games of all time on Metacritic. Credit: Mashable screenshot: Metacritic Critics have dubbed GTA 6 everything from "the single most impressive video game I have ever played" to "a masterpiece of open-world design." Meanwhile, players are spending their first few hours with the game and reacting in real-time . GTA 6 is out now and from every angle, Mashable's got you covered . title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Ars Technica review
author: Kyle Orland
body: Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner. A tiny heart with a plus sign pops up, showing that our relationship is stronger for this quotidian domestic effort. This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI , a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple. The reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installment received a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers. body: Nvidia held its Q3 2027 earnings call on Tuesday, less than a week after former CEO Jensen Huang resigned amidst reports he had engaged in multiple extramarital affairs including with an alleged Chinese spy . While Huang did not appear during the earnings call, he did publish a statement saying that he would happily return to his former role as Nvidia's CEO if asked. SEE ALSO: Who could replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia long-term? Here are the top contenders. The AI boom has sparked a significant spike in demand for computer components, leading to increasing profits for chipmakers such as Nvidia. Earlier this year, the company reported $81.6 billion in revenue during Q1 and $96.2 billion in Q2 . This growth has continued in Q4, with Nvidia announcing its quarterly revenue had increased by 20 percent to $115.8 billion. However, the elephant in the room was Huang, whose recent scandal and departure prompted a significant drop in Nvidia's stock . During Tuesday's earnings call, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones stated that Huang had voluntarily resigned on Nov. 12 "after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms." Nvidia is currently searching for a permanent CEO , with CFO Colette Kress acting in the role in the interim. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," said Jones. title: Hurdle hints and answers for November 18, 2026
body: If you like playing daily word games like Wordle , then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine. There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown. An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle. title: FAA official oversaw router work just before nationwide ground stop, report claims
body: An official with the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) was on the ground in Arkansas when new telecommunications wires were replaced, an action that preceded Friday's national ground stop by eight minutes, according to the Washington Post . The FAA official oversaw the work, tested it, and signed off on it, according to the Post 's report. The work involved replacing a router and swapping old copper wires for new fiber-optic cables, part of a national effort by the FAA to upgrade the airline industry's communication infrastructure. SEE ALSO: Apple confirms iCloud sign-in issues, App Store and Apple Pay outages The fact that an FAA official greenlit the work complicates Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's efforts to point fingers at L3Harris Technologies, a tech services provider and contractor tasked with updating the wires in Arkansas and leading the FAA's fiber-optic upgrades. Duffy said on Saturday that his agency is looking into whether "incompetence" by L3Harris led to the 4.5-hour ground stop. Responding to the Post 's request for comment, the FAA pointed to statements Duffy made on Tuesday in a news conference at the Capitol. During the conference, Duffy said that he wanted L3Harris to "hire better minds" for the wire replacement work and was considering bringing in new contractors to help. An exact cause for the communications outage has not yet been confirmed, an anonymous source told the Post . Duffy told reporters on Saturday that the replaced router in Arkansas was faulty and flooded the network with over 1,000 connection attempts every few seconds ,

title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
author: Nick Indge
body: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new "frontier ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. Because of these "recurring incursions," the state announced it would ban self-driving taxis from state freeways until the company implemented "effective corrective actions," the DMV said in a statement to TechCrunch. title: Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense
author: Stephen Clark
body: Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe's first true vertically integrated end-to-end space company. The announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio's shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo. title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
author: Dan Goodin
body: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword. Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript. Read full article Comments

title: OpenAI sued by California after admitting to 80 loss-of-control incidents
author: Jon Brodkin
body: California sued OpenAI yesterday, alleging it has tried to evade responsibility for the Hugging Face attack and about 80 other incidents in which the company lost control of its AI. The lawsuit was filed under the state's public nuisance and unfair competition laws. The July 2026 hack of Hugging Face and other attacks carried out by OpenAI's autonomous agents "may just be the tip of the iceberg," said a lawsuit filed in a state court by California Attorney General Rob Bonta. "OpenAI recently admitted to the Attorney General’s Office that it has lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing." OpenAI had publicly reported only 27 such incidents, showing that "OpenAI’s public reports do not represent the full scope of loss-of-control incidents involving OpenAI’s models that have impacted third parties," the lawsuit said. OpenAI "knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it," Bonta said in a press release . Read full article Comments

title: FEMA is testing the emergency alert system: Dont panic
body: If you hear an emergency broadcast this afternoon, don't panic! The Federal Emergency Management Agency ( FEMA ) and the Federal Communications Commission ( FCC ) are conducting a scheduled test of the national emergency alert system at 2:20 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 17. The FCC released a public notice about the scheduled test on Sept. 16, but it comes at a moment of high national anxiety, driven by recent tech outages among other troubling news stories. First, Microsoft suffered a widespread global outage on Thursday, Nov. 12, followed by a rare FAA nationwide ground stoppage the following day. And on Monday, a JPMorgan Chase outage sparked reports of a major bank outage (the problem was limited to Chase Bank and not a systemic issue or the result of a cyberattack), followed quickly by a United Airlines outage . None of these outages were directly related to or caused by cyberattackers, but the timing has sparked conspiracy theories and generalized anxiety. SEE ALSO: Trump says he takes 'no responsibility' for nationwide FAA ground stop However, the emergency alert was scheduled long before these outages; the FCC also announced a backup date of Dec. 3, in the event today's test does not occur. So, if your TV or radio suddenly goes into emergency mode today, don't freak out. FEMA will use the Integrated Public Alert and Warning System (IPAWS) to disseminate a message in both English and Spanish. title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design . The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app. The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road. As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You'll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It's under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy My Activity Other activity Gemini Apps Activity. Read full article Comments

According to the statement, U.S. agencies opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for "potential export control violations" after noticing suspicious activity. The Department of Commerce requested records from Nvidia regarding sales to Megaspeed in May 2025. (The export of advanced AI chips is highly regulated to protect national security, and Nvidia makes many of the chips that power the U.S. AI industry.) One month later, Nvidia put Megaspeed on its "no sell" list. That same month, U.S. agents and Singaporean law enforcement conducted an in-person investigation at Megaspeed and interviewed Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang. Following this on-site action, the Department of Justice "took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed," according to the statement. "While we don t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting," the joint statement says. Last week, Nvidia cofounder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company after he admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, who U.S. Intelligence alleges is a spy for the Chinese government. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life. To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled "Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech" on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki , a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts. title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
author: Dan Goodin
body: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user's knowledge. It’s “worse than a bug” Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent's reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. title: Sunrise on the Reaping review: The biggest and boldest Hunger Games yet
body: Are you looking for a movie to thoroughly wallop you? To leave you emotionally battered, physically exhausted, and full of despair and hope at the same time? Then allow me to prescribe a healthy dose of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , the sixth film in the Hunger Games series. Based on Suzanne Collins' second prequel novel following The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes , Sunrise on the Reaping once again rewinds the clock on Panem to the 50th Hunger Games, otherwise known as the Second Quarter Quell. These are the biggest Hunger Games yet, with 48 tributes instead of the standard 24. Among them is Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), future mentor to series protagonists Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark. SEE ALSO: The first 20 minutes of 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' blew me away The question here is not whether Haymitch will survive the games. We know, by virtue of the entire original trilogy, that he does. But before he was the cynical, heavy-drinking, lone wolf victor audiences met in The Hunger Games , he was an optimistic 16-year-old with a caring family, a loving relationship, and a solid community in District 12. So the real question of Sunrise on the Reaping becomes, what broke that young man down so thoroughly? The answer is, unsurprisingly, bleak as all hell. But director Francis Lawrence executes it in thrilling (if occasionally overstuffed) fashion, with a Hunger Games sequence that blows series-high Catching Fire 's own games out of the water, and a dogged focus on the philosophical themes at the core of Collins' work. title: Oura launches Jet Lag Plan, letting users hack their travel
body: Oura Ring users who are always on the go are about to benefit from a feature to combat jet lag. Jet Lag Plan is a new Oura feature that creates a plan to navigate time changes before, during, and after travel. We have all been there with travel. As much fun as the vacation is, if you're dealing with time zone changes, jet lag can totally kill the vibe. You don't want to waste a moment in a new place by taking a nap back at the hotel. Oura wants to help its Oura Ring users combat jet lag with its latest feature. The new feature is built off of a National University of Singapore study that used 1.5 million nights of sleep data from de-identified Oura users. Jet Lag Plan builds a plan designed just for you. It uses your flight itinerary along with your sleep patterns and chronotype to craft a series of recommendations. It produces a personalized schedule around sleep, light exposure, activity, and caffeine for journeys that cross three or more time zones. The feature uses Oura's AI-powered support, Oura Advisor, to adjust the plan as travel changes, in case things don't go as expected. Jet Lag Plan will be available globally to users with Gen 3 or newer hardware on both iOS and Android, as long as users have their language set to English. So if you're traveling for the holidays, don't let jet lag stop you from your vacation or family time. Opens in a new window Credit: Oura Oura Ring 5 $399 at Amazon Shop Now at Amazon
